summary: 1941 steel tower behind the Cumberland Court House, Virginia; state-administered and listed standing; 1937 report conflicts on build date; a 2019 visit found it unstaffed.

facts.design: four-legged steel structure about 85 feet high
facts.status_note: A photo caption says it is no longer used as a lookout and carries local government communications antennas.
facts.agency: Virginia Department of Conservation and Recreation

events.note: CCC camp item reports a 100-foot steel tower already constructed near the courthouse; conflicts with the Register's 1941 date
Steel tower built per the Register; 1941 Coast and Geodetic Survey describes a steel structure about 85 feet high
Steel tower replaced a wooden tower built in 1938 that was 66 feet tall with an 8x8 cabin
Registered June 9, 2015 as US 1082, VA 25; nominated by Krissy Reynolds
Register visit report of July 21, 2019 says the tower is not staffed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register dates the steel tower to 1941 after a 1938 wooden tower. A 1937 CCC camp item quoted on Forest Lookouts describes a 100-foot steel tower already built. The story reports both and does not choose.

The 1937 item says 100 feet, the 1941 survey says about 85 feet, and the photo caption says the lookout box is about 75 feet above ground. The record's 25.9 m (85 ft) follows the 1941 survey description.
The Register says the Department of Conservation and Recreation administers the tower; the photo title says Virginia Department of Forestry. The record keeps the Register's wording.

notes_for_editor: Standing comes from the Forest Fire Lookout Association list. The photo caption (Flickr, Earl C. Leatherberry) is the only source for no longer being used as a lookout, for the antennas, and for NRHP contributing status; Wikipedia's Cumberland Court House Historic District article and the DHR district page were checked and do not mention the tower. The 2019 unstaffed finding is from one visitor's report on the Register, not an official survey. Access is left out of facts: the Register's sign and directions fields say 'Unsure' and no source states public access. SAH Archipedia (VA-02-CB4) returned HTTP 403 and was not read. A Facebook post in Abandoned in Virginia mentions the tower; social media, not used. Brief's record height 25.9 m matches the 1941 survey; the 2015 registration and 1941 build year match the Register. No photos added: the Register credits a July 2019 photo to James Hull, but no image URL was read. Not verified: current use beyond the caption, owner's statement, antenna operators.
